text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

text: Thank you for confirming those symptoms; the sharp pain with specific movements strongly suggests a mechanical issue at the base of your thumb. I would like to perform a physical exam to confirm this, so I will request the results of a Finkelstein test. REQUEST TEST: Finkelstein_test.

text: RESULTS: Finkelstein's_Test: Positive, eliciting pain on the radial side of the wrist when grasping the thumb and exerting longitudinal traction towards the ulnar side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the positive Finkelstein test and your history of repetitive lifting, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis.
